intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 1F (CMT1F) is caused by heterozygous or homozygous mutation in the gene encoding the neurofilament light chain polypeptide (NEFL; 162280) on chromosome 8p21.

checks.claim: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 1F (CMT1F) is caused by heterozygous or homozygous mutation in the NEFL gene, which encodes the neurofilament light chain polypeptide.
checks.evidence_quote: Mutations in the neurofilament light chain gene (NEFL) cause early onset severe Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease.
checks.explanation: Abstract supports NEFL mutations causing CMT but does not mention CMT1F specifically or homozygous/recessive mutations.

checks.claim: The NEFL gene is located on chromosome 8p21.
checks.evidence_quote: Mutations in the NEFL gene were recently reported as a cause for autosomal dominant Charcot-Marie-Tooth type 2E (CMT2E) linked to chromosome 8p21.
checks.explanation: Chromosomal location of the gene is consistent with the stated linkage; standard nomenclature.

paragraphs.text: Jordanova et al. (2003) reported that mutations in the NEFL gene cause Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease with early onset and an often severe clinical phenotype, and with moderately to severely slowed nerve conduction velocities. In affected children described by Yum et al. (2009), there was slowly progressive atrophy and weakness of distal muscles of the feet and hands, bilateral pes cavus, and sensory impairment in a glove-and-stocking pattern, and nerve conduction velocities were markedly slowed into the 'demyelinating range.' Jordanova et al. (2003) noted that NEFL mutations had also been reported as a cause of autosomal dominant Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2E (CMT2E), linked to chromosome 8p21.

checks.claim: Mutations in the NEFL gene cause Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease with early onset.
checks.evidence_quote: Patients have an early onset and often a severe clinical phenotype.

checks.claim: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease caused by NEFL mutations often has a severe clinical phenotype.
checks.evidence_quote: Patients have an early onset and often a severe clinical phenotype.

checks.claim: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease caused by NEFL mutations shows moderately to severely slowed nerve conduction velocities.
checks.evidence_quote: Electrophysiological examination shows moderately to severely slowed nerve conduction velocities.

checks.claim: Children affected with NEFL-related CMT described by Yum et al. (2009) had slowly progressive atrophy and weakness of the distal muscles of the feet and hands.
checks.evidence_quote: All 4 affected individuals had hypotonia during infancy and early childhood, mildly delayed motor milestones, slowly progressive atrophy and weakness in distal muscles of the feet and hands, and bilateral pes cavus.

checks.claim: Children affected with NEFL-related CMT described by Yum et al. (2009) had bilateral pes cavus.
checks.evidence_quote: slowly progressive atrophy and weakness in distal muscles of the feet and hands, and bilateral pes cavus.
checks.explanation: Stated in the text. Note that Table 1 lists patient II-3 as not having pes cavus.

checks.evidence_quote: All have moderate sensory impairment in glove and stocking pattern.

checks.claim: Children affected with NEFL-related CMT described by Yum et al. (2009) had nerve conduction velocities markedly slowed into the demyelinating range.
checks.evidence_quote: As predicted, the reduced axonal caliber results in markedly slowed nerve conduction velocities well into the “demyelinating range”.

paragraphs.text: Jordanova et al. (2003) screened 323 patients with CMT or related peripheral neuropathies for NEFL mutations. Patients with NEFL mutations had early-onset and often severe disease. Electrophysiologic examination showed moderately to severely slowed nerve conduction velocities.

checks.evidence_quote: we screened 323 patients with CMT or related peripheral neuropathies

checks.evidence_quote: Patients have an early onset and often a severe clinical phenotype.

checks.evidence_quote: Patients have an early onset and often a severe clinical phenotype.

checks.claim: Electrophysiologic examination of patients with NEFL mutations in the Jordanova et al. (2003) study showed moderately to severely slowed nerve conduction velocities.
checks.evidence_quote: Electrophysiological examination shows moderately to severely slowed nerve conduction velocities.

paragraphs.text: Jordanova et al. (2003) found a de novo NEFL mutation in a patient with CMT and suggested that NEFL mutations be considered in patients with sporadic or dominantly inherited CMT. In the cohort studied by Abe et al. (2009), heterozygous missense mutations were found in 5 unrelated patients and a homozygous nonsense mutation in 1 other patient; Abe et al. (2009) concluded that nonsense NEFL mutations probably cause a recessive phenotype. Yum et al. (2009) found a homozygous nonsense NEFL mutation in a family with autosomal recessive CMT.

checks.claim: Jordanova et al. (2003) found a de novo NEFL mutation in a patient with CMT.
checks.evidence_quote: We report the first nerve biopsy of a CMT patient with a de novo missense mutation in NEFL

checks.claim: Jordanova et al. (2003) suggested that NEFL mutations be considered in patients with sporadic or dominantly inherited CMT.
checks.evidence_quote: we also suggest that NEFL mutations need to be considered in the molecular evaluation of patients with sporadic or dominantly inherited CMT.

checks.evidence_quote: We detected four heterozygous missense mutations--Pro8Leu, Glu90Lys, Asn98Ser and Glu396Lys--in five unrelated patients

checks.claim: Abe et al. (2009) concluded that nonsense NEFL mutations probably cause a recessive phenotype.
checks.evidence_quote: Results of our study show that nonsense NEFL mutations probably cause a recessive phenotype, in contrast to missense mutations, which cause a dominant phenotype.

checks.evidence_quote: We identified a two-generational family from Palestine in which CMT segregated as an autosomal recessive trait
checks.explanation: The paper describes a homozygous E210X nonsense mutation in this family with autosomal recessive CMT.

paragraphs.text: In patients with CMT or related peripheral neuropathies, Jordanova et al. (2003) identified 6 disease-associated missense mutations and a 3-bp in-frame deletion in the NEFL gene. Patients had early onset and slowed nerve conduction velocities. One patient had a de novo missense mutation in NEFL.

checks.evidence_quote: We detected six disease associated missense mutations and one 3-bp in-frame deletion clustered in functionally defined domains of the NEFL protein.

checks.claim: Jordanova et al. (2003) identified a 3-bp in-frame deletion in the NEFL gene in a patient with CMT or a related peripheral neuropathy.
checks.evidence_quote: We detected six disease associated missense mutations and one 3-bp in-frame deletion clustered in functionally defined domains of the NEFL protein.

paragraphs.text: Abe et al. (2009) found heterozygous missense mutations in the NEFL gene in 5 unrelated patients and a homozygous nonsense mutation in 1 other patient. This was the first report of a homozygous nonsense mutation in NEFL.

paragraphs.text: In affected children from a family with autosomal recessive CMT, Yum et al. (2009) identified a homozygous nonsense mutation in the NEFL gene. The resulting neuropathy was severe and of early onset.

checks.claim: Yum et al. (2009) identified a homozygous nonsense mutation in the NEFL gene in affected children from a family with autosomal recessive CMT.
checks.evidence_quote: All four affected children were homozygous for a nonsense mutation at glutamate 210 (E210X) in the NEFL gene; both parents were heterozygous carriers.
checks.explanation: Stated directly, and the paper also describes autosomal recessive segregation in this family.

checks.claim: The neuropathy caused by the homozygous NEFL nonsense mutation in the family reported by Yum et al. (2009) was severe.
checks.evidence_quote: resulting in a severe, early-onset axonal neuropathy with unique features

checks.claim: The neuropathy caused by the homozygous NEFL nonsense mutation in the family reported by Yum et al. (2009) had early onset.
checks.evidence_quote: Four of five siblings developed of a severe, progressive neuropathy beginning in early childhood.
